source: EDGAR, then one filing date changed by hand — see `planted` below

documents.date_basis: the latest filing whose facts this record contains; companyfacts is a catalogue of facts drawn from many filings and is not itself a filing

planted.what: one filing date, changed in a copy of tests/fixtures/CARR/companyfacts.json.gz so that a row the annual report filed is dated after the annual report — the row a run triggered by that report must not see
planted.why_that_date: 2026-04-30 is a date the record already carries: it is when the 10-Q filed the same period's total assets back. The newest filing date in this copy is therefore the same 2026-04-30 the committed record's manifest row records, so this directory's `filing_date` is the committed one and nothing about the record's own date is planted.
planted.what_it_judges: Carrier's 10-K was filed 2026-02-05 and this record is dated 2026-04-30, so a run triggered by the 10-K reads a catalogue dated after its own cutoff. Of the 12,011 rows, 11,676 are filed on or before 2026-02-05 in the committed record and 11,675 here: the one row of difference is the planted one, and it is the row that must not reach the reader.
planted.one_document_only: this directory holds the copied companyfacts record and nothing else, and the manifest records exactly that. The filings themselves stay under tests/fixtures/CARR/.
